findings.problem: organizational() serves WORKLIST batch-items (GET /batch-items and /batch-items/:id, routed from rait-worklist-scoped-reads.controller.ts:233/250) through a generic mapper. The mapper only strips tenant_id/snapshot/payload/grounds, so every response returns all inf.rait_batch_item columns: position, claim_due_on, accepted_at, declined_at, decline_kind, created_at and updated_at. The closed T0 map allows only id, case_id, batch_id and member_id for batch-items in every purpose (S/O/M/J), and says further functional fields need their own typed distribution contract. The generated WORKLIST commands OpenAPI also defines RaitBatchItemS/O/M/JRead with only those four properties and additionalProperties:false. The approved A2 packet treats batch position, deadline and acceptance as explicitly temporarily unavailable. So the runtime discloses distribution/position/deadline/acceptance data that the contract and Owner approval withhold, and the response does not conform to its typed schema. The preview's projectRaitBatchItem returns only the four fields, so preview/A2 tests hide this. No batch-items read assertion exists in rait-p402-scope.e2e.spec.ts.
findings.recommendation: Project batch-items through the closed FIELDS['batch-items'][purpose] allowlist, as read() does, using the complete case purpose already computed in SQL, instead of returning r.*. Add an Inspector HTTP+DB exact-key assertion for list and by-id batch-items for each served purpose. Add a runtime-vs-OpenAPI conformance check that covers the organizational() resources.

findings.problem: The unit-membership fallback for triage applies whenever hasRouting is false. hasRouting counts only active rait_case_pool_scope rows, active assignments and LOTE_ACEITO batch items. A case whose only exact pool link was explicitly revoked (active=false) is therefore treated as genuinely unlinked. Any same-unit, same-instance analyst or secretary in any pool regains triage purpose and triage/save-admissibility/admit/non-admission authority. The routing writer (rait-case-pool-scope.service.ts:41) treats a revoked row as an immutable disposition that blocks re-linking, so reads and writes treat revocation inconsistently. The e2e test 'admission preserves a revoked pool relation…' (rait-p402-scope.e2e.spec.ts:1869) relies on this widened fallback to admit. Legal admit must not gain a new routing guard. But using unit-wide inference after an authorized pool revocation goes beyond 'fallback only for genuinely unlinked cases' unless the Architect confirms it.
findings.recommendation: Have the Architect record whether a revoked-only link counts as unlinked for triage under T0. If it does not, include inactive links with nonempty provenance in hasRouting (fail closed to the revoked pool's members, or deny), without adding a legal admit guard. Add a second-same-unit-pool negative after revocation.

findings.problem: The new S1 scope pre-checks in WORKLIST and inquiry command paths bind caller IDs to uuid SQL predicates without validating the format first. Affected inputs: publish-schedule targetId (line 459); approve/accept/impediment/draw batch targetId (line 476); create-batch poolId in the member query and each caseIds element in the poolCaseSql check (lines 516/526); and inquiry targetId (rait-inquiry-command.service.ts:163). No 22P02 mapping exists in backend or @stynx-nyx, so a malformed ID returns HTTP 500 instead of a controlled 400/404. Main's later persist queries had the same pattern, but these new pre-checks now run first. The scope-read paths do validate correctly (404/400).
findings.recommendation: Reuse the UUID check before these queries: return 404 for path IDs and 400 VALIDATION_FAILED for malformed body IDs. Add malformed-ID HTTP negatives for one WORKLIST command and one inquiry command.

findings.problem: Scoped assignments reads filter only on the case purpose and pool/member consistency. An analyst whose M purpose comes from their own active assignment can therefore list every assignment row on that case, including other members' released assignments with member_id, assigned_by and release_reason. The T0 WORKLIST row says an active own assignment proves analyst/rapporteur purpose, 'not arbitrary other assignments'. This may be an over-disclosure under that wording; it needs source confirmation.
findings.recommendation: Have the Architect confirm whether own-assignment M/J purposes may read other members' assignment rows on the same case. If not, restrict the assignment rows (or release_reason/assigned_by) for those purposes, and add an Inspector negative.
